thread:
Priya: Heads-up from today's post-launch analytics: embedding latency for customer search rose from median 45ms -> 220ms during the 09:00 UTC traffic spike. Conversion on the search CTA dropped ~9%. We need to decide what gets hotfixed this week vs what we defer to next sprint. Proposing we use a simple prioritization rubric: (1) user-impact severity, (2) regression vs new, (3) customer-paid SLAs, (4) dev effort. Thoughts?

Ethan: Agreed on the rubric. Quick triage shows three candidates for Wave 0 (hotfix): 
- embedding RPC timeouts (affects search) 
- SSO token-refresh failing for some orgs (enterprise impact) 
- model-router fallback sometimes picks larger quantized model causing p99 latency blowouts
We should treat SSO as blocker for any org with 99.95 SLA violation.

Marina: From product POV, search is customer-visible and hurts activation. But SSO breaks sign-in for some customers1That might be higher priority for those orgs. Can we do a targeted patch for affected org_ids?

Jonah: Support queue: 7 enterprise accounts reporting SSO errors (Anil is PM for one); if we delay SSO fix we'll escalate. Customers asked for an ETA and mitigation.

Mei: For embedding timeouts my quick hypothesis: a new batching heuristic increased max waiting window causing long tail when bursty requests come. Short-term mitigation: cap batch wait to 3ms and increase fallback to synchronous small-batch path. Infrastructure work but low-risk. Dev estimate: 1.0d + 0.5d testing.

Anil: For SSO fallback we can add a token-refresh retry with backoff and a circuit-breaker. Small change in auth service, estimate 0.5d. However, we need security review sign-off if it touches token handling.

Ethan: Model-router fallback: bug is route comparator using approximate model size; when a quantized variant is considered "compatible" it sometimes increases decode time. Fix is nontrivial (~2d) because we need perf tests. Might be Wave 1.

Priya: Proposed decision (meeting): Wave 0 (this week) = embedding cap + SSO retry + short-term customer comms. Wave 1 (next sprint) = model-router comparator fix + perf regression hunt + more robust batching. Any objections?

Marina: OK. Can we define acceptance criteria for Wave 0 fixes so QA can greenlight a canary?

QA Bot: Suggested acceptance criteria template: 
- error rate delta <= baseline +0.2% over 2h (rolling)
- p95 latency for search <= baseline +150ms over 2h
- SSO success rate >= 99.9% for affected orgs over 1h
- smoke tests for sign-in, search, and timeline flows pass on canary (all green)

Ethan: I'll own embedding change + perf tests. Mei and Eng-Infra: can you prepare a canary routing that directs 5% traffic to the patched path and isolates affected regions? Example healthcheck curl we can use:
```
curl -s -H "x-customer-org: acme" https://api.redwood.internal/health/search | jq .latency_ms
```
We'll also use org-based routing for enterprise SSO to deploy the retry for just the 7 affected orgs first.

Mei: Yes, infra will create scope/route for org_ids: ["acme","borealis","greenleaf","anilco","helix","omega","lumen"]. Canary rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 4 hours if metrics meet the QA thresholds. I will add auto-rollback for p95+400ms or error_rate +0.5%.

Anil: I'll coordinate with the security reviewer for the token retry change. ETA for review: 6 business hours if we flag as high priority.

Jonah: I'll draft customer comms and put a temporary doc in the ACME CS folder. We'll proactively notify the 7 accounts with the mitigation plan and ETA.

Priya: Roadmap update: label the embedding work and SSO retry tickets as hotfix-this-week and move model-router comparator to enhancements-next-sprint. Also, add a follow-up ticket to run a thorough perf regression analysis across dev/prod model variants. Link: https://board.redwood/product/afterlaunch/1979234567

Ethan: Quick note on cost: capping batch wait will slightly increase per-token overhead in low-latency mode. Rough estimate +1.8% token cost at current QPS for the next 48 hours. Approve?

Priya: Approve for stability window. We can revert after Wave 1 optimizations.

Mei: Action items summarized: 
- Ethan: land embedding cap + perf tests (owner)
- Mei + Eng-Infra: canary routing and rollback rules (owner)
- Anil: security review for SSO retry (owner)
- Jonah: customer comms draft and notify enterprise (owner)
- QA Bot: run smoke + regression after canary (owner)
Target start: canary kickoff tomorrow 08:00 UTC.

QA Bot: CI snapshot: baseline test pass 112/116. Will prioritize smoke runs for canary targets.

Marina: Thx. Let's also capture the "definition of done" for each ticket: 
- embedding: deploy + metrics stable for 12h on canary + post-canary perf run.
- SSO: deploy retry + security sign-off + 24h monitoring.

Priya: Good call. We'll reconvene 2h after canary start for a status pulse. If canary fails auto-rollback and schedule postmortem. :white_check_mark:

Jonah: :thumbsup: I'll schedule the customer touchpoints and post the coms in #support.

Ethan: :rocket: starting work now, will post PR link when ready.

QA Bot: Smoke tests queued and will report to channel after run.

Priya: Thanks team. I'll update the roadmap board and ping execs with the mitigation note once canary is green.
